format.note: Required fields are present; the allocation-capture and reversal clauses form one end-to-end obligation. Activation facts align with given/when, examples are concrete, and observability labels are reasonable. The mechanical check passes with a nonblocking coder-text length warning.

generality.note: The rule addresses attributed multi-entry consumption across domains; booking and inventory examples illustrate the general shape without prescribing a particular application.

decisionUseful.note: Coder-facing text specifies durable allocation capture, restoration to original entries, injected-clock checks, restored/forfeited outcomes, idempotency, and critical-section discipline, with concrete implementation guidance and prohibitions.

extraObligations: verifier_detail requires forfeiture when an original entry no longer exists: 'If an original entry no longer exists or is no longer valid at reversal time, its amount is forfeited per domain policy and reported as forfeited'. The specification establishes policy-based forfeiture for entries no longer valid at reversal time, but does not establish that missing entries must be treated as forfeited rather than, for example, an integrity failure.

requiredFixes: Remove the mandatory forfeiture outcome for nonexistent original entries from verifier_detail. Retain the prohibition on replacement credits and the specified policy-based handling of entries no longer valid at reversal time, without prescribing an unspecified missing-entry outcome.
audit.summary: The convention is general, actionable, and covers all specified knowledge without task-specific leakage. It fails only because its verifier adds a mandatory missing-entry forfeiture policy not established by spec.md.
